name: @clawops/cli

tools.name: clawops_status
tools.description:
Get what is deployed for a clawops-managed stack: public IP, gateway URL,
SSH user, or that nothing is deployed yet. Reads stack outputs, and asks
the host only for requests its host agent left for the operator
(pendingHandoffs): each is a clawops command to show the user as it is.
A request clears when that command is run, or after 7 days.

Use when: the user asks what exists for a stack, where to reach it, or
whether its agent is waiting on them.

Do NOT use when: the user asks whether the gateway is actually WORKING —
that needs the host, so use clawops_doctor. Also not for live logs (use
clawops_logs_tail) or config values (use clawops_config_get).

stackName.description: Stack name. Defaults to active stack from config.

tools.name: clawops_doctor
tools.description:
Run clawops's diagnostics and return the report: Node and Pulumi runtime, config,
SSH key and known_hosts, cloud credentials per configured provider, and the
supported OpenClaw range. With stackName, also contacts the host for container
state, the deployed OpenClaw version, a real gateway health probe, whether the
port is published to the internet, disk usage on the state directory, log
rotation, and hardening drift.

Use when: something is not working and you do not yet know what; before any
deploy, upgrade or migration; or to find out which OpenClaw version a gateway is
actually running.

Do NOT use when: you already know the problem and want to fix it. This tool only
reports — it changes nothing, and never runs `openclaw doctor --fix`. To move a
gateway to another version, use clawops_gateway_update after clawops_backup_create.

Every check carries a status: fail (something is wrong that clawops can name),
warn (worth knowing, not broken), info (did not apply). `ok` is false only when
something failed — a fresh machine with no stacks is full of warnings and healthy.

stackName.description:
Stack to include remote checks for. Without it, only the local machine is
checked — no SSH connection is made.

failuresOnly.description: Return only failing and warning checks. Passing checks are counted, not listed.

tools.name: clawops_logs_tail
tools.description:
Tail recent gateway logs from a clawops-managed instance.

Use when: the user wants to investigate recent activity or errors, or
asks "what's been happening" on the gateway.

Do NOT use when: the user wants real-time streaming logs (those are not
well-suited to tool calls; suggest the user run `clawops logs -f` directly
in their terminal). Do NOT use for instance-level system logs: no tool runs
arbitrary remote commands, so tell the user to run `clawops ssh --command
'journalctl ...'` themselves.

stackName.description: Which stack's gateway to read. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

tailLines.description: How many of the most recent lines to return. Keep it small; output is trimmed to 8KB regardless

tools.name: clawops_monitor
tools.description:
Take a live snapshot of a running clawops stack: gateway health, container
status, resource usage (CPU, memory, disk), and recent log lines.

Use when: the user wants to know if the gateway is running, how much
memory or CPU it is using, what recent log activity looks like, or
wants a quick health overview richer than clawops_status.

Do NOT use when: the user wants real-time streaming logs (use
clawops_logs_tail or suggest `clawops logs -f`). Do NOT use for
configuration queries (use clawops_config_get).

stackName.description: Stack name. Defaults to active stack.

tailLines.description: Log lines to include in snapshot.

tools.name: clawops_config_get
tools.description:
Read a configuration value from the remote OpenClaw gateway.

Use when: the user wants to inspect current OpenClaw config (e.g., which
model provider is active, which channels are enabled).

Do NOT use when: the user wants to change the config — use
clawops_config_set instead.

stackName.description: Which stack's gateway config to read. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

key.description: Dot-path config key, e.g., gateway.auth.mode. Omit to dump the full config.

tools.name: clawops_agents_list
tools.description:
List agents currently registered on the remote OpenClaw gateway.

Use when: the user wants to see which agents are running, debug agent
routing, or count active workspaces.

Do NOT use when: the user wants one agent's activity — that is clawops_agents_logs.

stackName.description: Which stack's agents to list. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

tools.name: clawops_agents_logs
tools.description:
One agent's recent activity, read from the gateway's audit log, newest last.
Paginated: pass the returned cursor to continue.

Use when: the user asks what a specific agent did, or why it behaved as it did.

Do NOT use when: the user wants the gateway's own log stream — that is
clawops_logs_tail. Do NOT use to find agent names — that is clawops_agents_list.

stackName.description: Which stack the agent runs on. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

name.description: The agent's name, as clawops_agents_list reports it

limit.description: Maximum activity records to return. Omitted = 50

cursor.description: The cursor a previous call returned, to continue from where it stopped. Omitted = the most recent records

tools.name: clawops_gateway_status
tools.description:
Whether the OpenClaw gateway container is running, when it started, and which image it
runs, as docker reports it on the host.

Use when: the user asks whether the gateway is up or which OpenClaw version is deployed.

Do NOT use when: the user wants a full health check — clawops_doctor probes the gateway
itself rather than the container. Do NOT use to change anything; this only reads.

stackName.description: Which stack's gateway to inspect. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

tools.name: clawops_secret_list
tools.description:
List the secrets clawops stores locally, by name and status. Never returns a value.

Use when: the user asks which secrets are set, or before a deploy that references one.

Do NOT use when: the user wants to set or rotate a secret. No tool does that, because the
value would pass through the conversation (R6): ask the user to run
`clawops secret set <NAME>` or `clawops secret rotate <NAME>` in a terminal.

tools.name: clawops_secret_audit
tools.description:
Report secrets that stacks reference but clawops does not have, and `$secret:` references
that cannot be resolved. Never returns a value.

Use when: a deploy or config change fails on a missing secret, or before applying a plan
whose config references secrets.

Do NOT use when: the user wants to set the missing secret — ask them to run
`clawops secret set <NAME>` in a terminal; no tool takes a secret value (R6).

tools.name: clawops_up
tools.description:
Provision and deploy a clawops stack. Idempotent — re-running with no spec
change produces no diff. Long-running (median 3min, p99 8min) so emits
progress notifications per R12.

Use when: the user explicitly asks to deploy, provision, create, or "spin
up" a stack. Always after the user has reviewed a plan
(clawops_plan first when in doubt).

Do NOT use when: the user has not yet generated a plan and is in
exploratory/discovery mode — use clawops_plan first. Do NOT use for an
existing stack you only need to update; refresh first.

stackName.description: Name for the stack to provision, and the name every later command refers to it by. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

provider.description: Defaults to provider configured for this stack

region.description: Cloud region to deploy into, in the provider's own spelling (us-east-1, us-central1, eastus). Omitted = the region recorded for the stack

instanceType.description:
A clawops size (micro|small|medium|large|gpu) or a provider-native machine type.
Not an enum: Azure offers SKU families per subscription, and an account offered
none of the five sizes clawops names would otherwise have no way to deploy.

sshCidr.description:
CIDR(s) allowed to reach SSH, comma-separated, or 'auto' for the caller's own
address. Omitted means none, and nothing will be able to connect — including
every clawops day-two command.

gatewayCidr.description: CIDR(s) allowed to reach the gateway port. Requires publishGateway=all.

publishGateway.description: Which interface the gateway binds. 'all' serves plaintext HTTP.

dryRun.description: Show what would be created and change nothing. Use this first when the user has not yet approved a spend

tools.name: clawops_destroy
tools.description:
Destroy a clawops stack. Removes ALL provisioned resources. Triggers
elicitation confirmation showing the resource diff before execution
(R19). Cannot be undone.

Use when: the user explicitly asks to destroy, tear down, delete, or
remove a stack. Always confirm the stack name.

Do NOT use when: the user wants to stop the gateway temporarily — that is not
a destroy, and no tool stops a gateway; clawops_gateway_restart restarts it. Do NOT use when in doubt about which stack; list first with
clawops_stacks_list.

stackName.description: The stack to destroy. Required, and worth repeating back to the user before calling: this deletes every resource it provisioned

tools.name: clawops_apply
tools.description:
Apply a previously-generated Maker plan (deploy-plan.schema.json).
Deterministic — the plan describes exactly what will be created.

Use when: the user has a plan file path and wants to apply it. This is
the agent-friendly path for any deploy/destroy operation.

Do NOT use when: there's no plan file — generate one first with
clawops_plan.

yes.description: Skip the confirmation and apply immediately. Only when the user has already approved this specific plan

tools.name: clawops_plan
tools.description:
Generate a Maker deploy plan (does NOT apply). Plan is JSON conforming to
deploy-plan.schema.json — review before applying.

Use when: the user wants to see what would be created before committing,
or you (the agent) need a reviewable artifact for the user to approve.

Do NOT use when: the user has explicitly asked to deploy and you already
have their approval — go directly to clawops_up.

stackName.description: Which stack the plan is for. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

provider.description: Cloud to plan against. Omitted = the provider recorded for the stack. 'local' has no plan/apply path and is refused

region.description: Cloud region, in the provider's own spelling (us-east-1, us-central1, eastus). Omitted = the region recorded for the stack

instanceType.description: A clawops alias (micro|small|medium|large|gpu) or a machine type the cloud names itself, e.g. t3.small

sshCidr.description: CIDR(s) allowed to reach SSH, comma-separated, or 'auto' for this machine. Omitted = none, and nothing will be able to connect

gatewayCidr.description: CIDR(s) allowed to reach the gateway port, or 'auto'. Requires publishGateway=all

publishGateway.description: Which interface the gateway binds. loopback (default) keeps it off the network

privateOnly.description: Close public SSH and gateway access; reach the stack over its tailnet. Requires a verified tailnet address (clawops_harden with tailscale), and refuses unless that address answers SSH now

outPath.description: Absolute path to write plan; if omitted, plan returned inline

tools.name: clawops_config_set
tools.description:
Set a configuration value on the remote OpenClaw gateway. Optionally
restarts the gateway after.

Use when: the user wants to change OpenClaw configuration (model
provider, channel auth, gateway port).

Do NOT use when: the user is reading config — use clawops_config_get.
Do NOT bulk-edit; one key at a time so changes are auditable (R21).

stackName.description: Which stack's gateway config to write. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

key.description: Dotted path into the gateway config, e.g. models.provider or channels.slack.enabled

restart.description: Restart the gateway so the change takes effect. Without it the value is written and the running gateway keeps the old one

tools.name: clawops_config_unset
tools.description:
Remove a configuration key from the remote OpenClaw gateway config, reverting
it to the OpenClaw default.

Use when: the user wants to delete a config key entirely (e.g., remove a
channel, clear an override).

Do NOT use when: the user wants to set the key to a new value — use
clawops_config_set instead.

stackName.description: Which stack's gateway config to write. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

restart.description: Restart the gateway so the removal takes effect. Without it the key is removed and the running gateway keeps the old value

tools.name: clawops_config_validate
tools.description:
Validate the remote OpenClaw gateway config against the known schema. Checks
for structural errors (wrong types, unknown top-level keys) that would cause
OpenClaw to fail on startup.

Use when: the user wants to verify config before restarting the gateway, or
after editing openclaw.json manually.

Do NOT use when: the user wants to change config — use clawops_config_set.

stackName.description: Which stack's deployed config to validate. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

tools.name: clawops_gateway_restart
tools.description:
Restart the OpenClaw gateway daemon on the remote instance.

Use when: a gateway-wide config change requires reload, or the gateway is
reported as unresponsive.

Note: OpenClaw 2.0 removed per-agent restart; `gateway restart` is the only
restart it offers, and it affects every agent on the host. Brief downtime (~10s).

stackName.description: Which stack's gateway to restart. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

tools.name: clawops_gateway_update
tools.description:
Move the gateway to a different OpenClaw version: pull the image and restart the gateway
on it. Every agent on the host restarts with it.

Use when: the user asks to upgrade or downgrade OpenClaw on a running stack, naming a
version.

Do NOT use when: the user has not named a concrete version — moving tags such as
`latest` are refused, as the CLI refuses them. Do NOT use without a backup the user can
return to: suggest clawops_backup_create first.

stackName.description: Which stack's gateway to update. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

version.description: A concrete OpenClaw version to move to, e.g. 2026.9.2. Moving tags are refused

yes.description: Skip the confirmation. Only when the user has already approved this specific update

tools.name: clawops_backup_create
tools.description:
Take a backup of the gateway's state (config, database, sessions, transcripts and
installed plugins) and download it to a local archive. Live state is not changed.

Use when: the user asks for a backup, and before anything that replaces state: a
version update, a migration, a restore, or a plan that replaces the instance.

Do NOT use when: the user wants to back up cloud infrastructure — Pulumi state and plans
cover that, not this.

stackName.description: Which stack to back up. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

out.description: Absolute local path to write the archive to. Omitted = a timestamped file under ~/.clawops/backups

tools.name: clawops_backup_restore
tools.description:
Verify a backup archive and expand it on the host beside the live state, never over it.
With activate: true, also put it into service: stop the gateway, swap the restored state
in (keeping the state it replaces), restart, and roll back if the gateway does not answer.

Use when: the user asks to restore or recover from a backup, naming the archive.

Do NOT use when: the gateway is merely unhealthy — clawops_workflow_recover diagnoses that
without discarding state. Restoring is time travel: everything since the backup is lost,
and channel credentials may need relinking.

stackName.description: Which stack to restore onto. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

file.description: Absolute local path to the backup archive, as clawops_backup_create wrote it

activate.description: Put the restored state into service. Omitted = expand into a staging directory and touch nothing live

yes.description: Skip the confirmation. Only when the user has already approved this specific restore

tools.name: clawops_migrate
tools.description:
Move a deployment from OpenClaw 1.x onto the 2.0 runtime contract: state ownership,
config, and the gateway's run command, in the order a real migration showed works.

Use when: a stack still runs OpenClaw 1.x and the user wants it on 2.x. clawops_doctor
and clawops_gateway_status say which line a stack runs.

Do NOT use when: the stack is already on 2.x — use clawops_gateway_update to change
versions within 2.x. Take a backup first with clawops_backup_create.

stackName.description: Which stack to migrate. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

openclawVersion.description: The OpenClaw 2.x version to migrate to. Omitted = the version this clawops release defaults to

yes.description: Skip the confirmation. Only when the user has already approved this migration

tools.name: clawops_secret_delete
tools.description:
Delete a locally stored secret by name. Warns when a stack still references it.

Use when: the user asks to remove a secret they no longer use.

Do NOT use when: the user wants to replace a value — ask them to run
`clawops secret rotate <NAME>`; no tool takes a secret value (R6).

name.description: The secret's name, as clawops_secret_list reports it

yes.description: Skip the confirmation. Only when the user has already approved this deletion

tools.name: clawops_init
tools.description:
Register a stack and write ~/.clawops/config.json: the provider, the state backend, the
region, and an SSH key pair generated if one is not already there. Nothing is provisioned
and nothing is charged; this only creates local configuration.

Use when: any other clawops tool reports that there is no config, or the user wants to add
a second stack alongside the ones they have. This is the first call on a machine that has
never run clawops — a fresh container, a new laptop, a sandbox.

Adding a stack is additive and safe: existing stacks are kept. Overwriting one needs
force: true, because changing a state backend orphans the Pulumi state it points at — the
infrastructure stays up and clawops can no longer see or destroy it.

For aws, gcp and azure, stateUrl can be omitted and clawops names a bucket from the
account it can see; that needs cloud credentials in the environment, so in a sandbox pass
stateUrl explicitly. The local provider needs host instead, and no cloud account at all.

Do NOT use when: the user wants to deploy — that is clawops_up, after this. Credentials
are never passed here: clawops reads them from the environment (R6).

provider.description: Which cloud this stack deploys to, or 'local' for a machine you already have

stackName.description: Name for the stack, used by every later call. Omitted = "default"

stateUrl.description: Where Pulumi state lives, e.g. s3://bucket/clawops, gs://bucket/clawops, azblob://container. Omitted = clawops names one from the cloud account it can see, which needs credentials

region.description: Cloud region in the provider's own spelling. Omitted = us-east-1 (aws), us-central1 (gcp), eastus (azure)

host.description: [local only] Hostname or IP of the machine to manage. Required when provider is local

sshUser.description: [local only] SSH login user. Omitted = root

force.description: Overwrite a stack that already exists. Refused without it, because replacing a state backend orphans the state it points at

tools.name: clawops_harden
tools.description:
Apply security hardening to a deployed stack: SSH, UFW, fail2ban,
unattended-upgrades, the Docker socket, and per-cloud checks. Optionally join
the stack to a Tailscale network and reach it there instead of over the public
internet.

Use when: the user asks to harden, secure, or lock down a stack; asks what the
hardening report says (with dryRun: true, which changes nothing); or asks to put
a stack on their tailnet.

tailscale: true installs Tailscale, joins the tailnet as clawops-<stack>, and
then moves clawops onto that address — but only after opening an SSH session to
it, against host keys pinned over the connection already trusted. If that fails,
nothing is recorded and the public address stays in use. The auth key comes from
`clawops secret set TAILSCALE_AUTH_KEY` and is never passed through this tool
(R6).

tailscaleRevert: true takes the host back off the tailnet, over its public
address. On a private-only stack it refuses and names the plan/apply commands
that reopen SSH first — relay them rather than trying to work around it.

To close the public ports afterwards, plan with privateOnly: true and apply that
plan; this tool does not change firewall rules.

Do NOT use when: the user wants to know whether a stack is healthy — that is
clawops_doctor. Do NOT pass tailscale and tailscaleRevert together.

stackName.description: Which stack to harden. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

options.description: Comma-separated module IDs; default is every defaultOn module for the provider

dryRun.description: Report the current state, change nothing

tailscale.description: Join the tailnet, verify this machine reaches the host there, then use that address

tailscaleRevert.description: Leave the tailnet and go back to the public address

tools.name: clawops_task_status
tools.description:
Poll the status of a long-running clawops task (returned by clawops_up,
clawops_destroy, clawops_apply, etc.). Per R12 streaming model.

Use when: the user is waiting on a long-running deploy/destroy and wants
progress, OR you need to check whether a previously-started operation
finished.

Do NOT use when: there is no active taskId — start the operation first.

taskId.description: The taskId returned by a long-running tool such as clawops_up, clawops_apply or clawops_destroy

tools.name: clawops_workflow_deploy_app
tools.description:
Single-tool workflow that takes a user from "I want to deploy OpenClaw
to <provider>" to a verified, healthy gateway. Internally: plan → user
confirms (elicitation) → up → wait for healthy → return URL.

Use when: the user expresses end-to-end deployment intent ("deploy to
AWS", "spin up an OpenClaw on GCP for me").

Do NOT use when: the user is mid-deployment and only needs one step
(e.g., they already have a plan; use clawops_apply). Do NOT use for
destroying or updating — separate workflows.

provider.description: Cloud to deploy to. Omitted = the default provider in ~/.clawops/config.json

region.description: Cloud region, in the provider's own spelling (us-east-1, us-central1, eastus). Omitted = the provider's default

stackName.description: Name for the new stack. Omitted = the default stack name in ~/.clawops/config.json

instanceType.description: Machine size: a clawops alias (micro|small|medium|large|gpu) or a type the cloud names itself, e.g. t3.small

tools.name: clawops_workflow_recover
tools.description:
Diagnostic workflow for an unhealthy stack. Internally: what is deployed
(clawops_status) → the stack's failed health checks (clawops_doctor) → the
gateway's last 50 log lines (clawops_logs_tail) → a report with next steps that
name the tool for each kind of failure. Changes nothing.

Use when: the user reports any "not working" symptom and you don't know
where to start. Best entry point for troubleshooting.

Do NOT use when: the user has already identified the problem and asks for
a specific fix.

stackName.description: Which stack to diagnose. Omitted = the default stack in ~/.clawops/config.json

tools.name: clawops_stacks_list
tools.description:
List all clawops-managed stacks across all configured providers.

Use when: the user wants an overview of their deployments, asks "what
stacks do I have", or wants to compare stacks before an operation.

Do NOT use when: the user named a specific stack — use clawops_status
directly with that name.

tools.name: clawops_stacks_delete
tools.description:
Remove a stack from ~/.clawops/config.json. This forgets the stack; it does not tear
down its infrastructure, and it refuses a stack that is still deployed unless forced.

Use when: the user wants to stop tracking a stack whose resources are already gone.

Do NOT use when: the user wants the infrastructure removed — that is clawops_destroy,
first. Forcing the delete of a deployed stack leaves resources running and billing that
clawops can no longer see.

name.description: The stack to remove from config, as clawops_stacks_list reports it

force.description: Skip the safety checks: allow deleting the default stack, or one still deployed. Omitted = refuse both

yes.description: Skip the confirmation. Only when the user has already approved this deletion
